key_insight: Suspicion around the use of generative AI in manuscripts is rising in academic publishing, risking unjust accusations and reactive policies; the paper calls for measured, evidence-based responses to avoid harming researchers and the scientific record.
problem_solved: Clarifies the challenge of growing generative-AI suspicion—uneven detection practices, policy confusion, and potential harms from false positives—by diagnosing causes and proposing balanced editorial and community responses.
method: Qualitative review of recent editorial practices, public cases, and policy statements in academic publishing.
Critical analysis of the rhetoric, detection tools, and procedural responses that drive suspicion and its consequences.
Synthesis of recommendations for evidence-based, fair editorial workflows and guidance for authors and institutions.
impact: Alerts AI/ML practitioners and publishers to the risks of over-reliance on imperfect detectors and ad-hoc policies; encourages transparent, fair processes that protect research integrity while enabling responsible use of generative tools.
visual_elements: Timeline showing rise in reported suspicion incidents and corresponding policy shifts across journals
Flowchart of an editorial decision process with recommended verification steps and appeals path
Side-by-side graphic illustrating limitations of common detection methods (false positives vs false negatives)
Stakeholder map (authors, editors, institutions, toolmakers) with recommended roles and responsibilities
paper_title: On the troubling rise of generative AI suspicion in academic publishing
